Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: schedule_create
tools.description: Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence as scheduledAt in UTC and scheduledAtLocal in the zone of rrule. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes.

rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

target.description: this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory and preset. With this_session or new_once, a delivery waits until the previous one finishes, and only the latest occurrence that passed meanwhile is delivered. Use this_session for reminders and for follow-ups to this conversation; use new_once or new for independent work, such as a recurring report, and whenever the user asks for a new conversation.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. Supply `provider` and `model` together. Omitted values use child defaults, falling back to compatible parent values. When the effective route changes, an omitted `reasoning_effort` uses the model's default.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

<content>
1: # StreamTranslator V1.3 — Sentence-Level Translation Grouping
2: 
3: ## Overview
4: 
5: V1.2 segments audio by time (VAD endpoint or `hardMaxSegmentMs`), sends each segment to ASR
6: independently, and translates each segment independently. When the speaker talks continuously
7: without natural pauses, `hardMax` cuts produce transcripts that begin mid-sentence with no prior
8: context. This causes confusing translations and a fragmented history view.
9: 
10: This spec introduces `TextSentenceAccumulator`, a component that buffers ASR output across
11: `hardMax` boundaries and flushes semantically complete sentences as translation units.
12: 
13: Floating-window real-time display is **unchanged**. History and translation are the two surfaces
14: that benefit.
15: 
16: ---
17: 
18: ## Problem Statement
19: 
20: Observed in a continuous-speech session (game reveal stream, 2026-08-04):
21: 
22: | Segment | CutReason | Source text (truncated) |
23: |---|---|---|
24: | Seq 1 | SilenceDetected | "…Train Sim World Six will be coming on September 2025." |
25: | Seq 2 | HardMax | "**Five**, coming with a top-notch selection…" |
26: | Seq 3 | HardMax | "**The free starter edition.** So the free starter pack…" |
27: | Seq 4 | HardMax | "Train Sim World Journey. …**The free start.**" |
28: | Seq 5 | HardMax | "**The free starter pack** will be available…" |
29: 
30: Each segment is translated in isolation. "Five," has no context; "The free start." is a
31: mid-sentence truncation. The translation model cannot recover semantic continuity.
32: 
33: The **ASR accuracy problem** (each chunk transcribed without audio context from prior chunks)
34: requires streaming ASR and is deferred. This spec addresses the **translation unit problem**
35: and **history coherence problem**, both fixable at the text layer.
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## Design Goals
40: 
41: 1. History view shows sentence-complete entries instead of time-aligned fragments.
42: 2. Translation input spans one or more `hardMax` segments and ends at a sentence boundary.
43: 3. Floating window real-time display is unchanged (all ASR segments shown immediately).
44: 4. No new ML model dependencies; sentence detection uses punctuation heuristics.
45: 5. Force-flush threshold is user-configurable (default 350 chars, range 50–800).
46: 6. Source-language tail of the previous sentence unit is passed to the translation model as
47:    context (implements the "prior source context" improvement discussed during design).
48: 
49: ## Non-Goals
50: 
51: - Fixing ASR transcription accuracy at segment boundaries — requires streaming ASR (WebSocket);
52:   deferred pending a cost-effective API. `TextSentenceAccumulator` remains useful even when
53:   streaming ASR is added, as a fallback for segments that still need grouping.
54: - Speaker change detection (Layer 2); deferred to a later V1.3 iteration.
55: - ML-based punctuation restoration (e.g. `deepmultilingualpunctuation`); can replace the regex
56:   heuristic in a future patch without changing the accumulator contract.
57: - Streaming translation display.
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## Architecture
62: 
63: ### Current flow
64: 
65: ```
66: SubtitleRuntime
67:   └─ OnSubtitleReady(item)
68:        ├─ FloatingSubtitleWindow.PublishSource(item)   // real-time display
69:        ├─ SubtitleList.Items.Insert(0, item)            // history UI
70:        ├─ SubtitleHistoryStore.AppendAsync(item)        // persistence
71:        └─ TranslationSession.Submit(item)               // translation
72: ```
73: 
74: ### New flow
75: 
76: ```
77: SubtitleRuntime
78:   └─ OnSubtitleReady(item)
79:        ├─ FloatingSubtitleWindow.PublishSource(item)     // UNCHANGED — real-time
80:        └─ TextSentenceAccumulator.Add(item)
81:               │  (on SentenceUnitReady)
82:               ├─ SubtitleList.Items.Insert(0, unit)       // history UI — sentence units only
83:               ├─ SubtitleHistoryStore.AppendAsync(unit)   // persistence — sentence units only
84:               └─ TranslationSession.Submit(unit)          // translation — sentence units only
85: ```
86: 
87: `TextSentenceAccumulator` raises `SentenceUnitReady` when it decides a complete translation
88: unit is ready. The history list and translation session are now driven by this event, not by
89: raw `SubtitleReady`.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## CutReason Propagation
94: 
95: `CompletedSpeechSegment.CutReason` exists today but is not forwarded to `SubtitleItem`.
96: It must be added so the accumulator can distinguish forced from natural boundaries.
97: 
98: Add to `SubtitleItem` (Core project):
99: 
100: ```csharp
101: public string? CutReason { get; init; }
102: // Values: "SilenceDetected" | "SoftMax" | "HardMax" | null (legacy/unknown)
103: ```
104: 
105: Set it in `SubtitleRuntime.PublishTerminalResponseAsync` when constructing the `SubtitleItem`,
106: forwarding `segment.CutReason.ToString()`.
107: 
108: Accumulator flush rules by CutReason:
109: 
110: | CutReason | Accumulator action |
111: |---|---|
112: | `SilenceDetected` | Flush immediately — natural speech boundary |
113: | `SoftMax` | Flush immediately — soft segment limit with some silence |
114: | `HardMax` | Accumulate; apply sentence boundary check |
115: | `null` / unknown | Flush immediately (safe default) |
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## TextSentenceAccumulator
120: 
121: ### Responsibilities
122: 
123: - Receive `SubtitleItem` instances from `SubtitleRuntime`.
124: - Buffer items whose `CutReason` is `HardMax`.
125: - Detect sentence boundaries in the accumulated text.
126: - Emit `SentenceUnit` events representing semantically complete translation units.
127: - Force-flush when the buffer exceeds the configured character threshold.
128: 
129: ### State
130: 
131: ```csharp
132: private readonly List<SubtitleItem> _buffer = [];
133: private string _previousSentenceSourceTail = "";  // context for translation
134: private int ForceFlushThreshold => _settings.Translation.SentenceAccumulationLimit;
135: ```
136: 
137: ### Processing algorithm
138: 
139: ```
140: Add(item):
141:   1. Append item to _buffer.
142:   2. If item.CutReason is NOT HardMax  →  Flush("natural")
143:   3. Else:
144:        combinedText = string.Join(" ", _buffer.Select(x => x.SourceText))
145:        boundary = SentenceBoundaryScanner.FindLast(combinedText)
146:        if boundary found:
147:            sentenceText  = combinedText[..boundary]
148:            remainderText = combinedText[boundary..].TrimStart()
149:            Flush("sentence", upTo: boundary)
150:            RetainRemainder(remainderText)
151:        else if combinedText.Length >= ForceFlushThreshold:
152:            Flush("force")
153: ```
154: 
155: ### Flush output — SentenceUnit
156: 
157: ```csharp
158: public sealed record SentenceUnit
159: {
160:     public string SourceText { get; init; }          // combined sentence text
161:     public TimeSpan Start    { get; init; }          // earliest contributing segment
162:     public TimeSpan End      { get; init; }          // latest contributing segment
163:     public DateTimeOffset GeneratedAt { get; init; } // latest timestamp
164:     public string UtteranceGroupId { get; init; }    // last contributing group id
165:     public string[] ContributingGroupIds { get; init; }
166:     public string PreviousSentenceSourceTail { get; init; } // last ~100 chars of prior unit
167:     public string FlushReason { get; init; }         // "natural"|"sentence"|"force"
168: }
169: ```
170: 
171: `SentenceUnit` is converted to a regular `SubtitleItem` (with `Type = "sentence_unit"`)
172: before being passed to history and translation — no schema changes to downstream consumers.
173: 
174: ### Remainder attribution after sentence split
175: 
176: When a sentence boundary splits a buffer item's text (the boundary falls inside one item's
177: `SourceText`), that item is partially consumed. The implementation:
178: 
179: 1. Remove all items whose full text is consumed by `sentenceText`.
180: 2. Trim the last partially-consumed item's `SourceText` to the remainder slice.
181: 3. Keep it in the buffer as the first item of the next accumulation cycle.
182: 
183: This approximation is acceptable because partial items are short tail fragments that gain
184: full context in the next sentence.
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## Sentence Boundary Detection
189: 
190: `SentenceBoundaryScanner` is a static helper in the Core project.
191: 
192: ### Algorithm
193: 
194: ```
195: FindLast(text):
196:   candidates = all matches of regex [.!?][ \t]+[A-Z]  (position of the space/tab)
197:   for each candidate (right to left):
198:       wordBefore = last word ending at the punctuation mark
199:       if wordBefore.Length <= 2            → skip (abbreviation: "Mr.", "St.")
200:       if wordsInSentence(text, candidate) < MinSentenceWords (default 5) → skip
201:       return candidate position
202:   return -1  (no boundary)
203: ```
204: 
205: ### Known limitations (acceptable for V1.3)
206: 
207: - Decimal numbers ("9.30") and URLs are treated as sentence ends if followed by a capital
208:   word. False positive rate is low in conversational English ASR output.
209: - Non-English source languages with different punctuation conventions are not handled.
210:   A punctuation restoration model can replace this scanner in a future patch without
211:   changing the accumulator contract.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: ## Settings Changes
216: 
217: ### New setting: translation accumulation threshold
218: 
219: | Field | Value |
220: |---|---|
221: | Location | Settings page → 字幕翻译 card |
222: | Label | 翻译积累上限（字符） |
223: | Control | `NumberBox` |
224: | Range | 50 – 800 |
225: | SmallChange / LargeChange | 50 / 100 |
226: | Default | 350 |
227: | Caption | "积累更多内容再翻译可提升连贯性，但会增加翻译延迟。" |
228: | AppSettings path | `Translation.SentenceAccumulationLimit` (int) |
229: 
230: The setting participates in the existing auto-save debounce (800 ms) and is persisted in
231: `settings.json`. Schema version bumped to **5**.
232: 
233: ### Schema migration
234: 
235: On load, if `schemaVersion < 5`, set `Translation.SentenceAccumulationLimit = 350`.
236: 
237: ### Existing setting: hardMaxSegmentMs
238: 
239: Already present in Settings → 音频 → "最长片段 (ms)", `HardMaxSegmentBox`,
240: range 6 000 – 20 000 ms, default 10 000. No change needed.
241: 
242: ---
243: 
244: ## Display Model Changes
245: 
246: ### Floating window
247: 
248: `FloatingSubtitleWindow` continues to receive `SubtitleReady` for every ASR segment.
249: No change. HardMax continuation fragments appear and are replaced in real time as usual.
250: 
251: **Pending-translation state for HardMax segments**: floating window entries that are
252: absorbed by the accumulator will never receive a `translatedText` update. In V1.3 this
253: gap is accepted — the floating window shows original-language text for those entries.
254: A future improvement could mark them with a visual "⌛" indicator.
255: 
256: ### History list
257: 
258: `SubtitleList` is populated from `SentenceUnitReady` instead of `SubtitleReady`.
259: Each history entry corresponds to one complete sentence (or a force-flushed unit).
260: The view shows fewer but more coherent entries compared to V1.2.
261: 
262: ### History persistence
263: 
264: `SubtitleHistoryStore` receives the `SentenceUnit`-derived `SubtitleItem`
265: (`type = "sentence_unit"`). The JSONL format is the same. V1.2 history files
266: (`type = "subtitle"`) continue to load and display correctly — no migration.
267: 
268: ---
269: 
270: ## Translation Context
271: 
272: When `TranslationSession.Submit` is called with a `SentenceUnit`-derived item:
273: 
274: - `sourceText` is the combined sentence text (unchanged field).
275: - The existing `context` list of recent translated entries is passed (unchanged).
276: - **New**: `PreviousSentenceSourceTail` (last ≤ 120 characters of the prior sentence unit's
277:   source text) is appended to the translation worker's prompt as a `previous_source` hint.
278: 
279: Translation worker prompt template gains an optional `previous_source` section:
280: 
281: ```
282: [If previous_source is non-empty]
283: Previous transcript (source language, for context only — do not translate):
284: {previous_source}
285: 
286: Translate the following:
287: {source_text}
288: ```
289: 
290: This is the "Option A" prior-source-context improvement scoped to sentence units, which is
291: more effective than per-segment context because the unit boundaries are now linguistically
292: meaningful.
293: 
294: ---
295: 
296: ## Data Model Summary
297: 
298: | Change | Scope |
299: |---|---|
300: | `SubtitleItem.CutReason` (nullable string) added | Core |
301: | `Translation.SentenceAccumulationLimit` added to `AppSettings` | Core |
302: | Schema version: 4 → 5, migration adds default value | Core |
303: | `SentenceUnit` record | App (Runtime) |
304: | `TextSentenceAccumulator` class | App (Runtime) |
305: | `SentenceBoundaryScanner` static helper | Core |
306: | Translation worker prompt template: optional `previous_source` | Python |
307: 
308: ---
309: 
310: ## Test Considerations
311: 
312: ### Unit tests — `SentenceBoundaryScanner`
313: 
314: - Full sentence ending with `. ` + capital → finds boundary.
315: - Abbreviation `"Mr. Smith"` → not a boundary.
316: - Sentence shorter than `MinSentenceWords` → not a boundary.
317: - Multiple sentences in text → returns last valid boundary.
318: - No boundary in text → returns -1.
319: 
320: ### Unit tests — `TextSentenceAccumulator`
321: 
322: - Single item with `CutReason = SilenceDetected` → immediate flush, no buffer.
323: - Two HardMax items forming one complete sentence → flush on second item.
324: - Three HardMax items, sentence boundary in second → flush after second, third retained.
325: - Buffer exceeds `ForceFlushThreshold` without boundary → force flush.
326: - Remainder text carries into next cycle correctly.
327: 
328: ### Integration
329: 
330: - `SubtitleItem.CutReason` is set for all three cut types in runtime tests.
331: - `SentenceAccumulationLimit` round-trips through settings save/load (schema v5 migration).
332: 
333: ### Smoke test
334: 
335: Run `ui-store-shell-smoke.ps1` after the change. Verify:
336: - Floating window still shows real-time per-segment subtitles.
337: - History list entries are coherent sentences (manual inspection).
338: - No regression in subtitle copy / clear history flows.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## Open Items
343: 
344: 1. **Floating window pending-translation indicator** — HardMax segments absorbed by the
345:    accumulator never get a `translatedText`. Consider a "⌛" visual marker in a follow-up.
346: 
347: 2. **Non-English source language punctuation** — The regex scanner is tuned for English.
348:    If the source language is Chinese, Japanese, or Korean, sentence-ending characters differ
349:    (`。？！`). Extend `SentenceBoundaryScanner` when non-Latin source languages are added.
350: 
351: 3. **Streaming ASR re-evaluation** — When a WebSocket-capable ASR API becomes cost-effective,
352:    `TextSentenceAccumulator` transitions from primary segmentation logic to a fallback for
353:    segments that still arrive as complete chunks. The component interface is unchanged.
354: 
355: 4. **Speaker change detection (Layer 2)** — Provides an additional `SpeakerChange` flush
356:    signal to the accumulator. Deferred; no interface changes needed at this layer to add it.

lines.text: V1.2 segments audio by time (VAD endpoint or `hardMaxSegmentMs`), sends each segment to ASR
independently, and translates each segment independently. When the speaker talks continuously
without natural pauses, `hardMax` cuts produce transcripts that begin mid-sentence with no prior
context. This causes confusing translations and a fragmented history view.
This spec introduces `TextSentenceAccumulator`, a component that buffers ASR output across
`hardMax` boundaries and flushes semantically complete sentences as translation units.
Floating-window real-time display is **unchanged**. History and translation are the two surfaces
Observed in a continuous-speech session (game reveal stream, 2026-08-04):
| Seq 1 | SilenceDetected | "…Train Sim World Six will be coming on September 2025." |
| Seq 2 | HardMax | "**Five**, coming with a top-notch selection…" |
| Seq 3 | HardMax | "**The free starter edition.** So the free starter pack…" |
| Seq 4 | HardMax | "Train Sim World Journey. …**The free start.**" |
| Seq 5 | HardMax | "**The free starter pack** will be available…" |
Each segment is translated in isolation. "Five," has no context; "The free start." is a
mid-sentence truncation. The translation model cannot recover semantic continuity.

requires streaming ASR and is deferred. This spec addresses the **translation unit problem**
and **history coherence problem**, both fixable at the text layer.

context (implements the "prior source context" improvement discussed during design).

<skill_instructions>
# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt clich�� or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from �� a design for a toy for girls aged 8�C11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence �� like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment �� one page-load sequence or one reveal �� lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 �� Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A �� B �� C'); labels built as 'WORD �� fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '��' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly �� the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4�C6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief �� revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it �� a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

/frontend-design Hi，这是我的一个开发项目，主要是提供非wss/realtime，基于MAD的语音转字幕+翻译程序。当前界面是基于WPF-UI实现的，包括悬浮窗，但UI的使用便利性、视觉美观性能否帮我看看还能不能更上一层楼？可以的话，给我一些相关的提升改进方案？
=== [88] assistant/message (role=assistant) ===
通读了你现有的 [MainWindow.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml>)、[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml>)、[App.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/App.xaml>) 及 [ui-polish-review-2026-07-26.md](<docs/ui-polish-review-2026-07-26.md>)。

你已经把基础工程品质打得很扎实了（WPF-UI + Mica、ContentDialog 统一、防抖自动保存、悬浮窗位置记忆、状态分类枚举、AutomationId 覆盖都到位了）。现在界面处在**“工整的工程工具”**阶段——要想在**使用便利性**和**视觉美感**上跨进**“让人一眼觉得精致、用起来完全不费心”**的档次，核心不在于加特效，而在于解决**产品特性与界面结构之间的错位**。

---

## 一、现状诊断：为什么当前 UI 还没“更上一层楼”

1. **视觉上是“平铺的表单”，缺少一个音频字幕软件该有的主角**
   - [MainWindow.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml>) 全站都套用同一个 [PanelBorder](<src/StreamTranslator.App/App.xaml#L44-L51>)，主页、设置页、关于页的视觉重量完全一样。
   - 主页上半截是静态字段 + 一根 8px 细蓝进度条，中间是 7 个纯文字格子（4×2 网格右下角还空一格），最下方还常驻一张写着“问题：无”的大卡片（[MainWindow.xaml:320-339](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml#L320-L339>)）——95% 正常运行时间里，主界面很大一块被“无”字占着。
2. **高频操作与低频参数没有分层**
   - 看直播/网课最高频的动作是：**启停、锁定悬浮窗、快速开关翻译/切目标语言、微调字号/透明度、切换输出设备**。但目前“锁定悬浮窗”藏在设置页滚动半屏之下，想切设备或关翻译也要切出主页去翻设置。
   - 顺手看到两处现存小瑕疵：
     - 主页的“悬浮窗”按钮在 [UpdateFloatingWindowButtonState](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L2146-L2154>) 中只换了图标和 Tooltip，按钮文案始终是静态的“悬浮窗”，状态不够直观。
     - “关于”页点击“复制诊断信息”调用 `TryCopyTextAsync`，成功提示写到了 `SubtitleHistoryCopyStatusText`（[MainWindow.xaml.cs:564-591](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L564-L591>)），但在“关于”页时历史页是隐藏的，用户点完没有任何成功反馈。
3. **悬浮窗缺少“就地操控”与针对非 Realtime（VAD 切段）模式的心理反馈**
   - 悬浮窗（[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml>)）目前是一块纯黑蓝圆角矩形，没有悬停微控条、没有右键菜单；右下角 `ResizeMode="CanResizeWithGrip"` 还会露出 Windows 经典灰点缩放角标，在深色半透明面板上非常违和。
   - **VAD 断句模式有一个天然特性**：说话停顿 300–600ms 后才切段送 API，再等 0.8–2s 出字幕。这段静默窗口期如果悬浮窗毫无动静，用户极易怀疑“是不是断了/没收到音”。
4. **设置页是一根超长滚筒，缺少预览与渐进披露**
   - 6 张大卡片、600 行 XAML 垂直堆叠，新手必配的 API Key 和硬核参数（最长片段、并发、带数学公式的翻译积累上限）混排在一起，认知负担重；调悬浮窗字号/透明度时没有实时预览舞台，只能把两个窗口错开对比。

---

## 二、确立视觉与设计 Token（定制方案）

针对“Windows 桌面实时音频捕获 + 双语字幕投射”这个品类，建议把视觉人格定为：**声学演播台（主控） × 影院无扰字幕条（悬浮窗）**。不脱离 Windows 11 原生 Fluent/Mica 体系（保证低维护成本与浅/深色天然融洽），但通过克制的声学指示色、清晰的信息层级和“一处动态焦点”拉开质感差距。

### 1. 色彩系统（叠加在 WPF-UI 原生 Mica 语义 Token 之上）
| 角色 | 浅色模式 | 深色模式 | 用途 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **监听激活色 (Live Signal)** | `#0F9D76` | `#2DD4A3` | 运行中徽章、VAD 触发高亮、收音电平中段 |
| **处理/翻译等待 (Pipeline Warm)** | `#D97706` | `#F5B041` | 识别中/翻译队列中、VAD 采样提示 |
| **峰值/异常告警 (Peak / Fault)** | `#C42B1C` | `#F87171` | 音频过载尖峰、链路故障节点 |
| **影院字幕底板 (Overlay Ink)** | `#0F141B` (78% alpha) | `#0F141B` (78% alpha) | 悬浮窗默认暗玻璃底板，比纯黑更柔和 |
| **译文强调色 (Subtitle Focus)** | `#FFF6D6`（可选暖白） | `#FFFFFF` / `#FFE8A3` | 在双语字幕中用色温/明度而非仅靠字号区分原译文 |

### 2. 排版与细节原则
- **数字防抖**：所有动态数字（电平百分比、延迟 ms、字幕时间戳、队列数）统一开启 `Typography.NumeralAlignment="Tabular"`，数字变化时字符不会左右跳动。
- **双语阅读权重反转能力**：看外语直播/课程时，用户第一眼要读的往往是**译文**，原文是辅助核对。悬浮窗应把**字体粗细、字号、明度**作为“主次语言”的变量，而不是写死“原文白亮粗、译文灰暗小”。
- **动效克制**：只在**音频电平与 VAD 收音状态**以及**新字幕柔和浮现**这两处保留微动效，避免给每张设置卡片加花哨悬停特效。

---

## 三、五大核心模块的升级方案

### 升级一：悬浮字幕窗——从“透明文字框”升级为“影院级可呼吸字幕条”
> **优先级最高**，因为用户 90% 的使用时间只盯着这个窗口。

1. **悬停微控胶囊栏（Hover Pill Bar）+ 右键菜单**
   - **默认态**：完全干净，只有字幕与底板，不遮挡视频。
   - **悬停态（仅未锁定时）**：鼠标移入悬浮窗顶部边缘时，在字幕上方居中淡入一条极细的半透明操作胶囊（180ms 淡入，移开 300ms 淡出）：
     ```text
             ╭──────────────────────────────────────────╮
             │  ⠿ 拖动  |  A-  A+  |  双语▾  |  🔒 锁定  | ⚙ │
             ╰──────────────────────────────────────────╯
     ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     │  刚才那一句会被柔和降暗到 58% 不透明度，不抢当前视线        │
     │                                                          │
     │  This is the latest caption recognized via VAD.          │
     │  这是最新识别并翻译出的当前字幕，保持 100% 清晰焦点        │
     └─────────────────────── ━━━ ──────────────────────────────┘
                              ▲ 2px 声学收音/识别微光指示条
     ```
   - 右键菜单同步提供：锁定（点击穿透）、显示模式（双语译文主 / 双语原文主 / 仅译文 / 仅原文）、预设皮肤切换、恢复默认居中、打开主窗口。
2. **专为 VAD 模式设计的“底部 2px 声学微光条”**
   - 静默时不可见；检测到人声（VAD Active）时，底边居中亮起一段随音量轻微伸缩的柔光细线；正在等待 ASR/翻译返回时，细线缓慢呼吸滑动。
   - 极度克制不刺眼，却彻底消除非流式识别时的“是不是卡死了”焦虑。
3. **双语视觉层级与新旧句焦距**
   - **焦点衰减**：显示 2–3 条字幕时，**最新一条 100% 不透明度，历史条降至 55%–65%**，眼球永远自动锁定最新内容。
   - **4 种展示模式一键切换**：`译文优先（译文大亮、原文小淡）` / `原文优先` / `仅译文` / `仅原文`。
   - **入场平滑**：新条目增加 160ms 的 `Opacity 0→1` + 4px 轻上移，译文到达时从“译文占位呼吸点”淡入替换，消除生硬闪烁。
4. **多画面可读性皮肤预设 + 隐形边缘缩放**
   - 内置 3 套一键预设（用户仍可微调透明度）：
     - **影院暗玻璃**（默认）：深蓝灰半透明底板 + 细微 1px 顶部高光描边（`#33FFFFFF`）。
     - **亮底高对比**（适配白底 PPT / 文档 / 网页会议）：更高不透明度深色底或文字外描边（自定义 `OutlinedText` / 多向阴影），确保纯白画面下同样锐利。
     - **极简浮字**（适配游戏 / 电影全屏）：底板透明度可拉至 `0%`（当前最小值限制在 `0.35`），靠强文字描边保证可读性。
   - **去掉 `CanResizeWithGrip`**：改用无视觉污染的左右边缘透明 HitTest 区域调整宽度（悬停左右边沿才显示微弱竖线提示和 `SizeWE` 光标），同时修正 `MaxHeight` 按当前所在显示器工作区计算，而非只取主屏。

---

### 升级二：主页重构——从“状态表格”升级为“轻盈演播控台”

当前主页大面积是静态文字，且正常态下底部“问题：无”非常空洞。建议重排为**三层结构**：

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 实时字幕                                     [● 监听中 · 均衡 400ms]    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ┌─ 演播控制带 (Hero Stage) ───────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │  [ ■ 停止字幕 ]   [ 👁 隐藏悬浮窗 ]  [ 🔒 锁定 ]                     │ │
│ │                                                                     │ │
│ │  输出设备 [ 扬声器 (Realtek) ▾ ] [↻]    翻译 [● 开启 → 中文 ▾]      │ │
│ │                                                                     │ │
│ │  输入电平  ▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯▯  54%  ● 检测到人声      │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                         │
│ ┌─ 运行链路 (Pipeline Strip) ─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │  (●)音频捕获 ──▶ (●)VAD断句 ──▶ (●)语音识别 ──▶ (●)字幕翻译 ──▶ (●)输出 │
│ │    监听中         400ms自适应     DeepSeek      队列 0 · 正常    双语  │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                         │
│ ┌─ 实时字幕监视器（最近 4 条）────────────────────────── 查看全部历史 ┐ │
│ │  18:36:12  We're switching to the new VAD endpoint model.           │ │
│ │            我们正在切换到新的 VAD 断句模型。                         │ │
│ │  18:36:05  Let's check the latency metrics first.                   │ │
│ │            我们先看看延迟指标。                                      │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│  (仅当有错误或翻译降级告警时，在链路下方以紧凑 Alert Banner 滑出)        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**具体收益：**
- **高频动作一屏直达**：在主页就能直接切换输出设备、一键开关翻译与改目标语言（停止态可切，运行态锁灰并提示原因）、切换悬浮窗显隐和锁定状态，无需来回切设置页。
- **声学电平仪升级**：把 8px 细蓝 `ProgressBar` 换成 **24–32 格分段式 LED 电平条**（绿 → 琥珀 → 红峰值衰减），旁边紧贴一个 `检测到人声 / 静音` 状态点。看一眼就能确认声音有没有进来、VAD 有没有正确触发。
- **运行链路图形化**：把原来的 4×2 纯文字格合并为**一条从左到右的 5 节点数据流**，和 [README.md](<docs/README.md#L47-L54>) 里写的工作原理完全一致。每个节点自带语义状态圆点（灰未启动 / 绿正常 / 琥珀队列中 / 红异常），一目了然定位卡在哪个环节。
- **消灭“问题：无”常驻卡**：无问题时不占位；一旦出错，在控制带下方滑出高对比度告警条，并附带直接操作按钮（如“前往设置检查 API Key”或“复制诊断信息”）。
- **主页内嵌迷你实时字幕流**：不用切页面也能边调参数边看识别效果，点击单条可直接复制。

---

### 升级三：设置页重构——分 Tab 减负 + 专家参数折叠 + 悬浮窗实时画布

当前的 [SettingsPage](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml#L465-L1062>) 把所有内容堆在一条 600 行长滚动列表里。建议改为**页内顶部 4 个分段标签（Segmented Tabs）**：

| 标签 | 收纳内容 | 关键体验升级 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. 服务与翻译** | 识别服务（ASR）+ 字幕翻译模型列表 | 给 ASR 也补一个**“测试连接”**按钮（当前只有翻译有测试连接）；模型卡片里直接提供悬停/行内“编辑/测试/删除”，比底部 4 个孤立小图标按钮更直观；请求超时/最大并发/翻译积累上限收入 `ui:CardExpander`“高级调优”。 |
| **2. 音频与断句** | 输出设备 + 断句策略 | 断句策略的 4 段长文案改为**动态单条解释卡片**（选“均衡”就只展示均衡的特性与延迟区间条，界面清爽一半）；同时去掉 `Width="456"` 硬编码；最短/最长片段、自适应统计样本放入可展开的“进阶断句参数”。 |
| **3. 悬浮窗外观** | 皮肤预设、显示模式、字号、行数、透明度 | **卡片顶部内嵌一个“所见即所得”迷你预览舞台**（支持一键切换 `暗色视频底 / 亮色 PPT 底 / 桌面壁纸底`），拖动透明度、字号或切皮肤时不用找真实悬浮窗就能预览对比度。 |
| **4. 通用** | 主题外观、全局快捷键、系统托盘行为、诊断模式 | 快捷键用键帽样式展示（如 `[Ctrl]` `+` `[Alt]` `+` `[S]`），更易扫读；加入“最小化/关闭时收入系统托盘”开关。 |

---

### 升级四：字幕历史与系统托盘——打通日常完整闭环

1. **系统托盘（Tray Icon）**
   - 字幕开启后，主窗口其实不需要常驻任务栏。接入托盘图标后：
     - 图标带极小状态角标（绿点 = 监听中，灰 = 就绪，红 = 异常）。
     - 左键单击快速呼出/隐藏主窗；右键直接控制：`开始/停止字幕`、`显示/隐藏悬浮窗`、`锁定/解锁悬浮窗`、`退出`。
2. **字幕历史页升级（[SubtitleHistoryPage](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml#L344-L463>)）**
   - **日期切换**：底层按天存 `yyyy-MM-dd.jsonl` 已就绪，在“今天”标题处换成日期下拉/前后翻日控件即可浏览往期记录。
   - **即时搜索 + 导出**：顶部加一个紧凑 `ui:TextBox`（带搜索图标）按关键字过滤；把“复制选中 / 复制最近 10 条 / 复制全部”收敛为更干净的**拆分按钮或精简操作组**，并新增**导出为 `.txt` / `.srt`（带时间戳）**。
   - **阅读体验细节**：
     - 给 `SubtitleList` 换 `ObservableCollection<SubtitleItem>` 确保 UI 虚拟化，且在用户向下滚看旧字幕时**暂停强制顶移**，在顶部浮出一条 `↑ 3 条新字幕` 胶囊按钮。
     - 每条字幕悬停时在右侧浮现一个轻量复制图标，不用先点选中再抬头点“复制选中”。
     - 统一把所有“复制成功”反馈（包括关于页的诊断信息）走底部 `Snackbar` 或带淡出的统一 Toast，彻底解决“关于页复制无反馈”的问题。

---

### 升级五：品牌识别度与精致感收口

- **极简应用图标**：设计一个几何感强的 `.ico`（例如：圆角深青蓝底 + 两条交错的字幕横杠与左侧声波弧线），同步放进 `ApplicationIcon` 和 `TitleBar.Header` 左侧（18×18），软件立刻从“开发中的原型”变成“成品软件”。
- **标题栏轻量化利用**：在 `TitleBar` 右侧（最小化按钮左边）可以放一个极轻的**当前状态/主题快切小按钮**或托盘收纳按钮，减少去设置页切深浅色的路径。
- **暗色模式细节走查**：检查 [MainWindow.xaml.cs:1656](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs#L1656>) 等动态创建控件处的兜底颜色，统一绑定 DynamicResource，确保浅/深色切换时零割裂。

---

## 四、建议的分阶段落地路线图

按**“用户体感提升 ÷ 改动成本”**排优先级，推荐分 4 步渐进推进，每一步都独立可发布、且兼容你现有的 UI 自动化测试（保留原有 `AutomationId`）：

| 阶段 | 核心交付 | 为什么先做 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Phase 1：悬浮窗质变** | 悬停微控胶囊条 + 右键菜单 + 双语显示模式（译文主/原文主/单语）+ 新旧句透明度梯度 + 底部 2px VAD 呼吸线 + 3 套可读性皮肤 + 去掉默认 ResizeGrip | 用户盯得最久，改完立刻有“专业桌面软件”的质感飞跃 |
| **Phase 2：主页演播台** | 顶部高频快捷控台（含设备/翻译/锁定同步）+ 分段 LED 电平仪 + 5 节点横向运行链路图 + 内嵌实时字幕预览 + 问题卡按需滑出 | 彻底甩掉“参数监控后台”观感，日常开播零切页 |
| **Phase 3：设置页减负 & 托盘** | 设置页 4 分段 Tab + `CardExpander` 折叠专家项 + 悬浮窗实时预览舞台 + 系统托盘常驻 + 修复关于页复制反馈 | 解决新手上手门槛和长时间挂后台的便利性 |
| **Phase 4：历史增强 & 品牌收口** | 历史日期切换、搜索、单条快捷复制、导出 `.srt`/`.txt`、回看防跳动 + 应用图标 | 补齐网课/会议/复盘用户的高频刚需 |

### 一、已完成的 Phase 1 升级内容

1. **悬停微控胶囊栏 + 深色玻璃右键菜单**（[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml>)、[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs>)）

   - 右键菜单同步提供上述全部操作，并支持一键**“重置位置到屏幕底部居中”**。
   - 悬浮窗内做的任何调整（字号、显示模式、皮肤、位置、宽度）都会**双向同步回主窗口设置页并防抖自动保存**。

2. **双语显示模式与新旧句焦点衰减**（[AppSettings.cs:144-182](<src/StreamTranslator.Core/Configuration/AppSettings.cs#L144-L182>)、[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs:546-690](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs#L546-L690>)）
   - 新增 4 种显示模式并持久化：
     - `双语 · 原文优先`（默认）：原文大亮、译文在下方；
     - `双语 · 译文优先`：译文暖白高亮为主焦点、原文略小且柔暗为辅，更贴合看外语直播/网课的阅读习惯；
     - `仅显示译文`（未开启翻译或译文未到位时自动回退显示原文，不出现空窗）；
     - `仅显示原文`。
   - **新旧句视觉层次**：同时展示 2–3 条字幕时，最新一条保持 `100%` 不透明度，上一条柔和衰减至 `62%`、再前一条 `44%`，入场自带 180ms 轻柔上浮，减少跳动感。

3. **底部 2.5px VAD / 识别活动微光指示条**（[RuntimeStatusUpdate.cs:18-37](<src/StreamTranslator.App/Runtime/RuntimeStatusUpdate.cs#L18-L37>)、[SubtitleRuntime.cs:196-205](<src/StreamTranslator.App/Runtime/SubtitleRuntime.cs#L196-L205>)、[FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs:238-285](<src/StreamTranslator.App/FloatingSubtitleWindow.xaml.cs#L238-L285>)）
   - 静默时自动隐藏；

   - **语音片段送往 ASR 识别中**时，切换为暖琥珀色（`#F5B041`）慢速呼吸灯；
   - 有效消除非 Realtime / VAD 断句模式下等待出字时的“是否断流/卡死”焦虑。

4. **3 套可读性皮肤预设 + 0%–95% 透明度范围 + 隐形边缘缩放**
   - 内置 **影院暗玻璃**（深蓝灰半透明 + 顶部 1px 渐变高光描边）、**亮底高对比**（适配白底 PPT / 文档会议）、**极简浮字**（超低底板不透明度 + 强化文字阴影，适配全屏视频/游戏）。

   - 移除违和的 Win32 默认 `CanResizeWithGrip` 灰点角标，改为左右两侧隐形缩放手柄（悬停时仅现一条极细竖线，拖动调整宽度并记忆位置）。
   - 修正了多显示器下的 `MaxHeight` 限高计算（改为按悬浮窗当前所在屏幕工作区计算，而非写死主屏）以及 x64 下 `GetWindowLongPtr/SetWindowLongPtr` 的点击穿透调用。

5. **主窗口联动收口**（[MainWindow.xaml:188-206](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml#L188-L206>)、[MainWindow.xaml:965-1042](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml#L965-L1042>)、[MainWindow.xaml.cs](<src/StreamTranslator.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs>)）

571:     {
572:         // SetDataObject with minimal internal retries so retry pacing stays under
573:         // ClipboardWritePolicy's control; Clipboard.SetText would add its own
574:         // ~1s of internal retries per attempt and delay failure feedback by seconds.
575:         var result = await ClipboardWritePolicy.TryWriteAsync(
576:             text,
577:             static value => System.Windows.Forms.Clipboard.SetDataObject(value, true, 1, 10));

581:             return;

<skill_content name="frontend-design">
<skill_resources>

<skill_instructions>
# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.
</skill_instructions>
</skill_content>
